name: Al-Farabi District
tagline: The central district with the parks and the square
description: The core of the city around Independence Park and the main square, with the government buildings, the theatres, the better hotels and the widest choice of restaurants. It is the most walkable part of Shymkent and where most visitors stay.
bestFor: Short stays and anyone without a car
pros: Parks, restaurants and hotels all close
cons: More expensive than the outer districts
Air quality drops sharply in winter

name: Abay District
tagline: The newer residential blocks north of the centre
description: The district north and west of the centre, holding much of the newer apartment construction that followed the city's promotion to republic status in 2018, along with shopping centres and a growing run of cafes.
bestFor: Longer stays wanting a newer flat with good internet
pros: Newest apartment stock in the city
Fast fibre in the new buildings

name: Enbekshi District
tagline: The bazaars and the working city
description: The northeastern district around the main bazaars, where the trade with Uzbekistan and the surrounding region actually happens. It is dense, cheap and entirely local, and the markets here are the best reason to visit Shymkent at all.
bestFor: Budget stays and anyone who wants the markets on the doorstep
pros: The main bazaars and the regional trade
The cheapest food and rents in the city
Genuinely local, with no visitor infrastructure
cons: No English and little patience for it

name: Karatau District
description: The large residential district in the south of the city, mostly Soviet-era blocks and newer private housing, with local markets and schools. Rents are among the lowest in Shymkent and it is where much of the working population lives.
bestFor: Long stays on a minimal budget with some Russian
cons: Nothing aimed at outsiders at all

name: Sayram
tagline: The ancient town on the eastern edge
description: A settlement about twelve kilometres east, one of the oldest continuously inhabited places in Kazakhstan and the birthplace of Khoja Ahmed Yasawi, with several mausoleums and a strongly Uzbek character quite distinct from the city.
bestFor: Anyone drawn to the Silk Road history rather than the city
pros: Genuine Silk Road history and mausoleums
cons: Conservative and quiet in the evening
